# Agent claim, implementation and handoff workflow

**AI disclosure:** This issue/document, including its title and all prose, was generated by AI at the repository owner's request.

This is the shared execution protocol for `iconidentify/libva-v4l2_request` and `iconidentify/omarchy-m1-video`. It supplements repository instructions; a ticket does not override AGENTS.md or grant permission for kernel changes, installation, module operations, reboots, desktop configuration changes or upstream reports.

## Choose work

1. Read the repository README, applicable AGENTS.md files, this workflow, the roadmap and the entire ticket. Driver work starts from `avd-fixes`; installer work starts from `main`.
2. Choose **one leaf ticket** labeled `status:ready`. Epics and the roadmap coordinate work and are not implementation claims. Prefer P0, then P1 within your skills and available equipment. The current ticket body and native blocked-by links are both authoritative; report inconsistencies before starting dependent work.
3. Read all comments, assignees, linked PRs and blockers. An unresolved prerequisite, required hardware or kernel authorization must be satisfied before the dependent action. A completed research ticket only unblocks implementation when its approved design establishes feasibility; it does not mean the feature exists.
4. Tickets marked `status:backlog` can be promoted when their prerequisites and resources are satisfied. Record that decision. Do not skip or remove dependency links merely to make a ticket claimable.


## Prepare work for distribution

A ready leaf must name its owning layer/files, public input revisions, a concrete
artifact, acceptance checks, required resources and the next action. Mark completed
prerequisites as completed in the body while retaining native dependency links.
A closed research dependency does not establish feasibility: name any remaining
contract or evidence gate. Do not use a generic "needs hardware" label as the only
explanation of why an offline deliverable cannot start.

Split an independently useful offline deliverable into a linked child when the
parent requires unavailable hardware or authorization. The child must be able to
finish against its own tests; do not quietly remove the parent's original gates.
Use native parent/sub-issue links and, where it gates the parent's implementation,
a blocked-by link from parent to child. Never make that child depend on completion
of its parent. Ready describes the bounded child, not the entire codec feature.

Contributors on non-Apple hosts may do source analysis and offline tests. Linux
is required for the V4L2 C build; no-device Python/source tasks can use any suitable
host. Do not run an installer or load a module to make an offline task claimable.

Status follows active work as well as blockers: keep a confirmed, unexpired
contributor claim visible as in-progress when a permitted scope is underway, with
unfinished gates stated separately. Do not distribute that scope to another agent.
A passing PR or merged partial contribution does not complete its parent. Mark
acceptance checkboxes only for the evidence actually delivered.

At each merge/handoff, reconcile direct dependents, native relationships, the live
roadmap and the canonical workflow issue. When this shared workflow changes,
update the driver guide and driver issue #8 together, and keep the companion
entry point consistent. Historical snapshots
stay labeled; the live queue remains authoritative.

## Claim without colliding

GitHub assignment alone is insufficient: several agents may share the same account. Use a unique session ID and preserve claims in comments.

Post a provisional comment with this structure:

```text
CLAIM
Agent/session: <unique session ID>
Ticket: <full issue URL>
Base commit: <SHA>
Branch/worktree: <branch and isolated local path>
Primary files/interfaces: <owned scope and expected overlaps>
Plan: <3-5 concrete steps tied to acceptance criteria>
Dependencies/resources checked: <links and evidence>
Hardware: none | <host/device; scheduling need>
Lease expires: <UTC timestamp, at most 24 hours ahead>
```

Then re-read the issue comments and open PRs. The earliest still-valid claim by GitHub server comment ID owns the ticket; later competing claims must withdraw before editing. This is an optimistic coordination convention, **not an atomic lock**. If ownership is ambiguous, resolve it in the issue with the other claimant/coordinator before touching overlapping work. Never overwrite another agent's branch or worktree.

After confirming ownership, assign the authenticated account when permissions allow and move the ticket to `status:in-progress`. Record the session ID even when every agent uses `@me`. An example after ownership is confirmed:

```sh
gh issue edit <number> --repo <owner/repo> --add-assignee @me \
  --remove-label status:ready --remove-label status:backlog \
  --add-label status:in-progress
```

One active implementation ticket per session. Renew your claim at each meaningful progress update and at least every four working hours, for no more than 24 hours ahead. Release explicitly when stopping. To take over an expired claim, first inspect the linked PR/latest comments and announce the takeover with a new session ID and branch. Preserve all prior work and state what will be reused; a stale timestamp never authorizes deleting it. A live PR or conflicting active work requires coordination.

## Isolate code and dependencies

- Use a dedicated worktree/branch, for example `agent/<ticket-number>-<short-topic>`, based on a freshly fetched default branch. Verify the worktree is clean before editing. Do not share a working directory between concurrent agents.
- List the actual files/interfaces you will change in your claim. Claims for different tickets do not grant ownership of the same shared core files. Coordinate `context.c`, `decode.c`, `surface.c`, `driver.c`, common test infrastructure, package pins and release docs before overlapping edits.
- Follow the ticket's owning layer. Driver fixes belong in the driver repo; kernel/system/client/display dependencies are tracked in the companion repo with exact external source revisions. Do not create a kernel workaround in generic VA code merely to avoid a dependency.
- Split an unexpectedly large ticket into linked implementation children before widening scope. Preserve the original acceptance criteria and dependency chain. Do not close a feature ticket when only its investigation is complete.

## Hardware is a separate exclusive resource

An issue claim does not reserve the decoder. Hardware commands go through
`python3 tests/hwguard.py -- <command>`, which holds an exclusive OS lock per
decoder identity. Never run two agents' tests simultaneously on the same host/decoder.

Hardware work requires read-only idle/fault preflight, finite deadlines, new-kernel-error/foreign-client monitoring, durable logs and an idle final state. Stop after a new decoder fault or wedge; do not reopen it repeatedly or unload/reload as automatic recovery. Keep tests on selected userspace builds using `LIBVA_DRIVERS_PATH` when possible.

The installer AGENTS.md requires a supported Apple Silicon/linux-asahi machine, explicit informed consent for installation, and saved work before module unload/reboot; it also says not to edit shipped patches. `needs:kernel-approval` identifies work that cannot proceed under those standing constraints without explicit scoped authorization. Design/source analysis can proceed independently. Keep OpenGL as the shipped mpv setting. Report setup problems in our repositories, not upstream.

Do not run untrusted PR code on a self-hosted hardware runner with host access or secrets. A host lock must be enforced by the runner/guard, independently of GitHub labels or comments.

## Implement and prove

1. Establish the smallest relevant baseline and reproduce a claimed bug before editing when feasible. Record source/tool/device identity. Avoid replaying a known firmware fault without a concrete fix.
2. Add a meaningful regression and implement the bounded fix. For new capability, prove truthful VA/V4L2 negotiation and full output correctness. Keep backend quirks scoped; do not add per-vector filename hacks.
3. Driver offline baseline:

   ```sh
   meson setup <fresh-build> -Db_sanitize=address,undefined
   meson test -C <fresh-build> --print-errorlogs
   sh tests/frame-check.sh
   sh tests/shared-contexts.sh
   ```

   The two shell commands without a driver argument are software checks. Hardware commands go through the guard. Installer offline baseline:

   ```sh
   bash -n install.sh uninstall.sh bin/apple-avd-rebuild tests/rebuild.sh libva/PKGBUILD libva/libva-v4l2_request-avd.install
   bash tests/rebuild.sh
   ```

4. Run ticket-specific checks and affected full codec suites. Compare exact passing-vector sets, not just totals. Preserve raw denominators, known failures and partial/aborted runs. Do not count software fallback as hardware success, 72,000 parser inputs as 72,000 independent tests, or correct decoded pixels as proof of correct display/boot behavior.
5. Provide source/package/driver hashes, dependency versions, device/kernel provenance, commands, expected/actual output, first differing frames when relevant, and guard/journal summaries. Keep private media, URLs, tokens, core dumps and unrelated process arguments out of public artifacts.

## PR, review and completion

- Open a scoped PR early as draft and link the ticket and dependency PRs. Include the problem, resulting behavior, meaningful before/after evidence, limitations and each acceptance criterion's status.
- The owner requested this disclosure for every AI-authored PR: **"This pull request, including its title and every word of this description, was generated by AI."** Preserve original authorship/credits for imported changes.
- Mark `status:review` when the concrete result and required evidence are ready. Passing CI alone does not satisfy missing hardware or release criteria. `avd-fixes` requires a PR, an up-to-date passing `userspace` check, and blocks force pushes/deletion, including for admins. Reviewer approvals are currently not mechanically required; this is not evidence of independent review.
- Prefer a separate agent/human review for shared lifetime, reference mapping, security, kernel and release changes when available; record whether review was independent. Never claim a self-check was independent review or bypass branch rules.
- Use `Fixes <full issue URL>` only for a fully completed leaf task. Use `Refs` for partial work, research parents, or cross-repo integration not yet validated. Default-branch auto-close must not hide unmet criteria.
- Close a task as completed only after its code/docs are merged into the owning default branch and all criteria have evidence. For research, attach the accepted decision and required implementation children; mark unsupported features honestly. A blocked or impossible implementation stays blocked or is explicitly closed as not planned with rationale, never as delivered support.
- Final handoff: commits/PRs, each criterion and evidence, tests not run and why, known risks, next exact command/step, active hardware processes/leases, and release/renewal of the claim. Update native dependencies and readiness on directly unblocked children. Epics close only when their promised outcomes and required children are complete.

## Status and priority meanings

- `status:ready`: scoped, prerequisites satisfied, claimable within listed permissions/resources.
- `status:backlog`: planned but outside the first wave or awaiting prioritization/resource arrangement.
- `status:blocked`: a named dependency, hardware/authorization or unresolved design prevents required work.
- `status:in-progress`: one identified agent owns active implementation.
- `status:review`: concrete result awaits review, checks or integration. Close only after acceptance.
- `priority:P0`: release-blocking correctness/safety or essential evidence infrastructure for the affected support claim.
- `priority:P1`: important compatibility, reliability or delivery work.
- `priority:P2`: extended coverage, optimization or hardware-dependent expansion.

Sizes S/M/L describe relative review scope, not promised hours. Hardware research is inherently uncertain. A status change must include the concrete reason when it alters another agent's ability to start.
